finding: At ctx=26800 and above, the DEFAULT (all-GPU KV, no --kv-placement) path fails at REAL context construction with a genuine Vulkan out-of-device-memory error while allocating compute buffers -- NOT a planner rejection, a real ggml_vulkan allocation failure -- even though gpu_policy's own pre-load ESTIMATE said the request should fit (this is exactly the 'pure KV-byte math can be false-safe' gap Phase 11/12 research already documented, now observed again from the product side). --kv-placement auto (which resolve_kv_placement() decides BEFORE llama_init_from_model() is ever called -- a pre-construction decision, not a post-failure or runtime relocation -- placing 2 of 28 layers' KV in CPU RAM for the single construction attempt that follows) and --kv-placement cpu (all 28 layers' KV to CPU RAM, decided the same way) both reliably SUCCEED at the exact same ctx/model/precision/weight-placement configuration.
reproducibility: Default failure at ctx=28500 reproduced twice (2/2 real Vulkan OOM). Auto success at ctx=28500 reproduced 3 times across this session (3/3 success, real generated text byte-identical each time).
